title: Automated Coverage-Based Testing of XACML Policies
algorithm_class: XACML modified condition/decision coverage (MC/DC); rule-pair coverage is a separate published criterion.
supported_guarantee: Original XPA MC/DC generator, Balana and Z3 reproduced all 28 condition-independence and 14 target-error obligations on conference3. The bundled 27 requests match author decisions; the rerun generated 25 requests.
limitations_vs_candidate: One static conference policy. The pinned October 2018 source postdates the June paper. Applying XPA to ordered histories needs a separately verified interface and a matched budget.
mechanism_analysis: The author implementation gives a reproducible static comparator for PolicyTrace. Each measured run used 25 solver invocations and 217 target evaluations before the 25 whole-policy decisions. Use those costs when designing the history comparison. All checked labels and run limits are in sacmat/xpa_execution/RESULTS.md.

title: XACBench: a XACML policy benchmark
algorithm_class: Benchmark-driven static XACML policy generation and evaluation profiles
supported_guarantee: Standard policy benchmark: profile-driven synthetic XACML policy/test generation with an evaluation harness for static policy structures (Crossref metadata verified 2026-11-15, issued 2020-04-21).
limitations_vs_candidate: Benchmark profiles address static policy documents: no delegation timelines, no revocation/redelegation/replay ordering, no cross-engine decision parity, and the ledger records an explicit scope difference from longitudinal traces; policy-profile pass-rate is a different endpoint from cross-engine non-parity on (history, request) units; no redistributable benchmark code is pinned in the registry.
mechanism_analysis: Strong benchmark baseline for SACMAT arm B2 and claim C2: XACBench owns profile-driven benchmarking of static policies, so the conformance corpus may claim novelty only as (policy history, request) pairs scored by cross-engine decision parity - if XACBench-style profile tests reproduce the same divergence classes without histories, C2 is not novel and the corpus is published as an incremental dataset. Registry entry xacbench-profile-driven-tests pins no redistributable benchmark code (Crossref-verified publication only); the profile translation into the portable four-valued oracle does not exist yet in evaluation/venue2027, so UNAVAILABLE_NOT_RUN is the honest status and it stays that way until a verifiable revision or a completed parity-checked profile translation exists.

title: Zanzibar: Google’s Consistent, Global Authorization System
algorithm_class: Consistency-aware distributed ReBAC authorization with zookie version tokens and global tuple-change ordering
supported_guarantee: Bounded-staleness permission evaluation via zookies/consistency tokens; monotonic per-user snapshot reads; externally consistent reads after tuple writes (Sec. 2.3-2.4) with planetary-scale production operation at Google; verified live at usenix.org 2026-11-15 (HTTP 200).
limitations_vs_candidate: Consistency governs permission-tuple evaluation only: no ordered-history conformance property, no four-valued decision oracle (NOT_APPLICABLE/INDETERMINATE), no purpose-bound delegation vocabulary on tuples, and no cross-engine parity measurement; a design paper with no official Google code release, so execution flows through the OpenFGA comparator row.
mechanism_analysis: Claim C3 design reference and the consistency-semantics comparator for RQ3: Zanzibar defines consistency-aware authorization (zookies, permission re-evaluation after relation changes) that PolicyTrace must not claim as novelty, but it offers no history-level conformance property - divergence here is measured at identical ordered histories and request attributes across real engine versions with untranslatable constructs labeled INDETERMINATE, never a consistency model. The paper is a design paper with no official code (honest UNAVAILABLE_NOT_RUN); its executable semantics reach the study through the pinned OpenFGA ORIGINAL_UPSTREAM row, and if disagreement disappears once histories are trivially linearizable, C3 collapses to a paper mapping and the Dataset/Tool claim is refused.

title: Cedar policy language and authorization reference implementation
algorithm_class: ABAC/PBAC policy-as-code evaluation engine with type-checked schema and formal validator
supported_guarantee: Executable fine-grained policy evaluation with type-checked schema, documented expressivity limits, and formal verification of the Cedar validator/converter; pinned at tag v4.14.1 (upstream revision 47d82a8293354f235d3f8d092c71071706401741, Apache-2.0, verified live via git ls-remote on 2026-11-15) as the Cedar half of registry baseline cedar-opa-policy-decision-nonce-registry serving the SACMAT Cedar encoding surface.
limitations_vs_candidate: Stateless per-request policy decision: no first-class delegation-chain or ordered-history construct, no consume-once state, no built-in temporal expiry semantics for delegation grants (must be encoded as attributes and re-checked by the caller), and no cross-engine conformance contract - its own upstream test suite validates engine-internal semantics, not a shared history corpus across engines (claim C8).
mechanism_analysis: RQ3 comparator engine 1 of 3 and claim C8 target: the pinned v4.14.1 engine receives the same synthetic (policy history, request) corpus through a frozen best-practice adapter, and conformance is measured as decision parity against the portable four-valued reference oracle - the engine executes its own semantics but holds no authority over ground truth, so engine-oracle mismatches are divergence witnesses, not labels. This is also the strongest-competing-explanation test surface: if residual cross-engine disagreement vanishes once Cedar encodings follow documented best practice, the encoding-artifact explanation wins and the paper reports portability limits instead of a fault-detection claim. Upstream revision resolved live via git ls-remote refs/tags/v4.14.1 on 2026-11-15.

title: OpenFGA: Zanzibar-inspired fine-grained authorization
algorithm_class: Zanzibar-inspired relationship-based authorization (ReBAC) with consistency tokens and fresh evaluation mode
supported_guarantee: Executable relationship checks with consistency tokens (minimize_latency=false) and fresh evaluation; pinned at tag v1.22.1 (upstream revision 44054f542f64e9b9589dd26a595081b3d2cfd942, Apache-2.0, verified live via git ls-remote on 2026-11-15) as registry baseline zanzibar-openfga - the SACMAT encoding surface for conformance testing per the shared baseline registry.
limitations_vs_candidate: Relationship-tuple consistency only: delegation chains are relations to be walked, but the engine has no ordered-history conformance property, no four-valued oracle, no purpose-narrowing vocabulary on tuples (must be encoded as relation attributes), and no consume-once semantics; its Zanzibar-style bounded staleness tolerates re-evaluation windows that ordered-history replay would expose, and its own test suite validates engine-internal semantics, not cross-engine parity.
mechanism_analysis: RQ3 comparator engine 2 of 3 and the executable Zanzibar-semantics surface: the pinned v1.22.1 server binary replays the same (policy history, request) corpus as Cedar and OPA under identical oracle adjudication, making relation-walked delegation the strongest ReBAC-style competing encoding - if OpenFGA reproduces every ordered-history decision the oracle labels, the conformance-corpus claim narrows to the engines that cannot express it. Untranslatable constructs are pre-labeled INDETERMINATE and excluded from parity denominators; adapter crash counts the arm as failed, never as DENY. Upstream revision resolved live via git ls-remote refs/tags/v1.22.1 on 2026-11-15.

title: Open Policy Agent (OPA): policy-as-code engine
algorithm_class: Rule-engine policy decision point (policy-as-code, Rego) with side-effect-free evaluation
supported_guarantee: Executable per-request policy decisions over arbitrary structured inputs; pinned at tag v1.22.4 (upstream revision ba39415db4b3c90cd68942a74b3cc2223ec2b23c, Apache-2.0, verified live via git ls-remote on 2026-11-15) as the alternative PDP recorded inside registry baseline cedar-opa-policy-decision-nonce-registry and the OPA encoding surface for SACMAT conformance testing.
limitations_vs_candidate: Stateless per-request evaluation: no built-in temporal consent, no delegation ancestry, no consume-once state, and no ordered-history construct - temporal precedence, revocation-before-replay and expiry races exist only if the caller encodes the entire history into the input document and re-derives semantics in Rego by hand, which is precisely the under-specification surface the study measures; upstream test suites validate engine-internal semantics only.
mechanism_analysis: RQ3 comparator engine 3 of 3: OPA's data-document input model makes it the sharpest test of the competing explanation that temporal faults are encoding artifacts - a Rego author can in principle encode any history semantics, so residual disagreement on identical best-practice encodings across OPA vs Cedar vs OpenFGA is direct evidence of semantic mismatch rather than expressivity gaps. Same-history parity failures with root causes attributed to semantic mismatch are the RQ3 endpoint; if OPA agrees with the oracle on every corpus unit, the divergence claim narrows accordingly and the corpus remains a tool-only contribution. Upstream revision resolved live via git ls-remote refs/tags/v1.22.4 on 2026-11-15.

title: Guide to Attribute Based Access Control (ABAC) Definition and Considerations
algorithm_class: Normative ABAC vocabulary and design guidance (standard)
supported_guarantee: Formal attribute-based access-control vocabulary (subject/resource/action/environment attributes including purpose-of-use) and policy-composition guidance; DOI resolves to the NIST CSRC publication (verified live 2026-11-15, HTTP 200); supplies the ABAC terms used to state the portable oracle encodings.
limitations_vs_candidate: Vocabulary and design considerations only: no algorithm, no history-sensitivity, no delegation-timeline semantics, no testing method and no measurement of divergence or detection - a standard cannot pre-empt a conformance-testing claim, and per claim C4 it fixes exactly the vocabulary whose ordered-history extension (fault taxonomy F01-F05) must be demonstrated as new.
mechanism_analysis: Claim C4 boundary comparator (nistabac): SP 800-162 defines the formal ABAC attribute vocabulary and policy-composition model that the synthetic corpus and four-valued oracle are phrased in, and it establishes that the standard itself contains no history sensitivity or testing method - so the fault taxonomy keyed on temporal precedence (F01-F05) is new only if single-request ABAC tests cannot reproduce it; if the taxonomy is reproducible from single-request tests, the temporal modifier is withdrawn. A normative standard has no runnable implementation to cite, so UNAVAILABLE_NOT_RUN is the correct status and it grounds vocabulary, never a runnable arm.

title: Elle: Inferring Isolation Anomalies from Experimental Observations
supported_guarantee: Infers isolation anomalies (G-anomalies, cyclic conflicts, lost update, write skew) from exported operation histories without instrumenting the system under test; pinned at tag v0.2.8 (upstream revision 2843344620c7d0653eef1c20728aa8580a05f505, EPL-2.0, verified live via git ls-remote on 2026-11-15) as the design precedent for history-checking instrumentation.
limitations_vs_candidate: Checks exported histories for concurrency anomalies: its anomaly algebra targets database isolation, not authorization semantics - no PERMIT/DENY/NOT_APPLICABLE/INDETERMINATE decision oracle, no policy-engine encodings, no metamorphic relation over consent delegation, and its findings presuppose a truthful, complete history export; the candidate's oracle is declared from declarative reference semantics, never inferred from observations alone.
mechanism_analysis: Methodological precedent for the trace-level checking instrument (not a baseline arm): Elle demonstrates that black-box history checking can expose state-space faults invisible to pointwise testing - the exact analogy PolicyTrace transfers from transaction histories to delegated-consent histories - while its limits mark what the candidate must add: a four-valued authorization oracle adjudicated against declarative reference semantics plus independent human review, not anomaly inference from observations. Pinned Elle v0.2.8 is recorded as instrument provenance; the SACMAT oracle never imports Elle, and an oracle importing candidate code would be disqualified per the SACMAT-scope stop-and-revise rule.

title: Uniform random authorization requests (blueprint arm B0; registry baseline uniform-random-authorization-requests)
algorithm_class: Uniform random request generation over the synthetic policy/principal graph; weak reference
supported_guarantee: Deliberately weak coverage reference: uniform sampling of requests over the synthetic policy/principal graph with matched oracle budget per SACMAT RQ2; anchors the low end of mutation score so every stronger arm's improvement is measurable against it.
limitations_vs_candidate: Weak by construction: uniform requests almost never land on zero-width temporal boundaries (revoke/request same tick, expiry racing decision time) or ordered-history faults, so it must never be presented as a competitor - the blueprint assigns it the weak-reference role only, and it lacks any history-aware generation.
mechanism_analysis: RQ1/RQ2 weak reference lower bound: registers the unmitigated random-generation mechanism whose expected mutant-kill rate calibrates the fault families; if B0 ever matches B3 or the PolicyTrace generator at equal budget, the experiment is misconfigured (the family structure would be saturated by chance) and the run is blocked rather than scored. The in-project generator does not exist yet in evaluation/venue2027 (registry entry upstream_revision UNAVAILABLE, notes: arm B0 weak reference; in-project; not yet run), so honestly UNAVAILABLE_NOT_RUN rather than claiming a run that never happened.

title: XACBench policy profile-driven synthetic tests (blueprint arm B2; registry baseline xacbench-profile-driven-tests)
venue: CLARA 2027 SACMAT blueprint (in-project translation of xacbench20)
algorithm_class: XACBench policy profile-driven synthetic test generation translated into the portable four-valued decision oracle (in-project translation of the published benchmark profiles)
supported_guarantee: Strong benchmark baseline: policy-profile-driven test generation executed against the study's ABAC encoding with profile pass-rate recorded under the portable PERMIT/DENY/NOT_APPLICABLE/INDETERMINATE oracle semantics; scope limited to static policy structures by the ledger's explicit scope difference.
limitations_vs_candidate: Static policy structures only: profile-driven tests have no delegation timelines, no revocation/redelegation/replay ordering, and no cross-engine replay - their endpoint is benchmark profile pass-rate, a different endpoint from cross-engine decision parity on (history, request) units, so the C2 claim survives only as corpus novelty, not benchmark novelty.
mechanism_analysis: Benchmark baseline for RQ2 and the C2 falsification arm: XACBench-style profile tests are run to check whether they reproduce the same divergence classes without histories - if they do, C2 is not novel and the corpus is published as an incremental dataset. No redistributable benchmark code is pinned in the registry (Crossref-verified publication only) and the in-project profile translation does not exist yet in evaluation/venue2027, so UNAVAILABLE_NOT_RUN is the honest status; it precludes comparative claims for the arm until a verifiable revision or a completed parity-checked profile translation exists (NOT_RUN_EXTERNAL discipline).

title: Property-based history generator without temporal metamorphs (blueprint arm B3; registry baseline property-based-history-generator-no-metamorphs)
algorithm_class: Property-based stateful history generation (hypothesis RuleBasedStateMachine) over policy/principal actions with deliberately no temporal metamorphic relation
supported_guarantee: Strongest stateful testing alternative: real hypothesis 6.167.1 engine (tag v6.167.1 -> commit a8dcd7422a325926693b5464f73349e361562b7c via git ls-remote 2026-11-15, MPL-2.0, installed version matches) drives RuleBasedStateMachine policy/principal actions against the same oracle budget; the arm runs the actual upstream engine, so its generation power is not a surrogate.
limitations_vs_candidate: Stateful but non-metamorphic: hypothesis explores action sequences and shrinks counterexamples, but it contains no temporal metamorphic relations - it can hit ordered faults (revocation-before-replay, expiry race) only by chance, with no mechanism that constructs the boundary ordering, and no cross-engine parity construction; minimal witness length is not optimized for fault classes, only for example size.
mechanism_analysis: Strongest competing baseline for RQ2 (novelty contract C5): the primary estimand is the paired mutation-score difference PolicyTrace minus B3 at equal oracle-call budget with family-clustered statistics - if B3 parity holds, the metamorphic mechanism claim is falsified in full. This is the only SACMAT arm with a pinned, verified, executable upstream implementation (ORIGINAL_UPSTREAM, available_code=yes): it runs the real Hypothesis engine at the pinned revision rather than a port, and its parity fixture (evaluation/venue2027/sacmat/fixtures/hypothesis_stateful_parity.json) plus exec_command are registered in the shared baseline registry; the in-project driver does not exist yet, so the arm is recorded honestly as not yet executed while the upstream pin is verified.

title: PolicyTrace temporal generator plus oracle (blueprint arm B4; the temporal-conformance candidate, not a comparator)
algorithm_class: Candidate: trace-level metamorphic test generation over ordered (policy history, request) units with portable four-valued oracle adjudication across Cedar/OpenFGA/OPA encodings
supported_guarantee: Claimed (not yet demonstrated): detection of trace-level fault families F01-F05 (expired delegate role, inheritance conflict, revoke-then-regrant ordering, nested-purpose mismatch, emergency override without approval obligation) that survive static coverage at equal oracle budget; cross-engine conformance divergence detection with INDETERMINATE pre-labeling of untranslatable constructs; minimal failure trace length as co-primary witness measure.
limitations_vs_candidate: It is the candidate itself, not a comparator: until SACMAT-rq_registry/oracle/dataset/baseline tasks land, no artifact exists, no run_id manifest exists, and every claimed guarantee is a prospective design commitment per the frozen novelty contract - this row exists to make the candidate auditable against the comparators above, never to assert results.
mechanism_analysis: Candidate arm B4 - the temporal-conformance candidate - recorded for falsification transparency: the mechanism (temporal metamorphs over grant/revoke/regrant/delegate/expire/request orderings adjudicated by an independent four-valued oracle that never imports candidate code) is exactly what RQ1-RQ3 require the B0-B3 arms and the B5/B6 no-history explanations to fail to deliver; the falsification rule binds the whole design - if the trace generator does not outperform B3 and B1 at equal oracle-call budget on the frozen corpus, the novel fault-detection claim is withdrawn and portability limits are published transparently. Until the candidate implementation exists in evaluation/venue2027/sacmat the honest status is UNAVAILABLE_NOT_RUN, and any invalid admission by the candidate on a history the oracle labels DENY falsifies the mechanism claim outright.

title: Static policy diff across engine encodings (RQ3 competing-explanation baseline from publication_overlap_registry)
venue: CLARA 2027 SACMAT overlap registry baseline (publication_overlap_registry.yaml, study sacmat)
algorithm_class: Static structural comparison of translated policy artifacts per engine (policy diff) without replaying any shared history
supported_guarantee: Competing-explanation baseline for RQ3: static policy diff predicts that comparing translated policy structures (rules, attributes, relations) across Cedar/OpenFGA/OPA encodings explains all observed divergence without ever replaying an ordered history into any engine; it is the overlap registry's first declared sacmat baseline and must be defeated, not strawmanned.
limitations_vs_candidate: Structural comparison cannot observe semantics: two encodings can be structurally identical yet diverge on ordered histories (combining-algorithm precedence vs relation-walk order, expiry boundary splitting, purpose-narrowing interaction with deny precedence), and structurally different encodings can be behaviorally equivalent - it yields no decision, no parity rate, and no INDETERMINATE labeling.
mechanism_analysis: RQ3 competing-explanation arm and the novelty-contract's strongest competing baseline for the conformance endpoint: the falsification condition is explicit - if residual cross-engine disagreement is fully explained by static policy diff, RQ3 reports zero-divergence and the conformance corpus is positioned as a tool-only contribution, never as a fault-detection claim. The diff tooling over frozen adapters does not exist yet in evaluation/venue2027 (the adapters themselves are pinned upstream but unbuilt), so UNAVAILABLE_NOT_RUN is honest; the arm must be built from the same frozen encodings the engines replay, never from a re-implementation under the same name (execution contract rule 8).

title: Single-engine per-engine testing (engine-native test suites; RQ3 competing-explanation baseline from publication_overlap_registry)
venue: CLARA 2027 SACMAT overlap registry baseline (publication_overlap_registry.yaml, study sacmat)
algorithm_class: Per-engine unit/property testing with each engine's own test discipline (Cedar/OpenFGA/OPA native suites), no shared corpus
supported_guarantee: Competing-explanation baseline for RQ3: single-engine testing predicts that each engine's own test suite plus per-engine unit tests explains all observed conformance behavior - engine-native suites validate engine-internal semantics thoroughly, which is exactly why they are the credible version of this explanation.
limitations_vs_candidate: Engine-native suites validate engine-internal semantics only (claim C8): there is no shared history corpus across engines, so same-history parity failures between engines under identical encodings are invisible by construction - a suite green on every engine says nothing about whether the engines agree with each other on the same ordered history.
mechanism_analysis: RQ3 competing-explanation arm and claim C8 falsification surface: the second overlap-registry sacmat baseline must be shown insufficient - if upstream suites already encode the shared corpus classes, C8 reduces to engineering integration work and the conformance-corpus novelty claim dies. The harness that replays engine-native test disciplines against the shared corpus does not exist yet in evaluation/venue2027, so UNAVAILABLE_NOT_RUN is honest; per-engine testing must be executed with each engine's real pinned binary (Cedar v4.14.1, OpenFGA v1.22.1, OPA v1.22.4), never mocked.
